posts.hook: Planning season isn't about picking tactics. It's about deciding what you actually believe your organization can do.
posts.direction: Angle: most orgs open a blank planning doc and immediately jump to channels and budgets — skipping the conviction layer that makes any plan hold. Cover: why strategy without belief collapses under pressure; why mission-driven orgs have an advantage here if they use it. Graphic: quote card — pull the core conviction as a bold centered statement.

posts.hook: 3 questions to answer before you write a single word of your 2027 marketing plan.
posts.direction: Angle: most plans start with tactics; these three questions force clarity on audience, message, and goal first. Cover: Who are we actually trying to reach? What one thing do we want them to do? What does success look like in plain language? Frame as pre-work, not extra work. Graphic: tip card with a numbered list — one question per row, brief annotation under each.

posts.hook: If you want 2027 to feel different, the work starts before the calendar flips. We can help you build the plan.
posts.direction: Angle: soft close on the planning-season theme — not pressure, but an honest invitation. Cover: name the specific help offered (clarity on message, channel selection, a plan that fits the org's actual capacity). End with a low-friction CTA — DM or link to a discovery call. Graphic: quote card with the hook as the hero line and a one-line CTA beneath.

posts.hook: Most organizations don't have a marketing problem. They have a clarity problem.
posts.direction: Angle: the real bottleneck isn't budget or tactics — it's not knowing what you're actually trying to say. Cover: unclear mission = unclear message = ignored content. Clarity is the foundation; everything else is decoration. Speak to churches and nonprofits who feel stuck. Graphic: quote card — bold central line, clean background, Bequest wordmark.

posts.hook: Before you plan next year's content, audit this year's message first.
posts.direction: Angle: a quick self-audit before 2027 planning locks in. Cover: three checkpoints — does your homepage say who you help and how, does your social bio match your current mission, does your call to action tell people exactly what to do next. Frame as a checklist anyone can run in an hour. Graphic: tip card with a numbered checklist, three items, clean layout.

posts.hook: A new year doesn't fix a foggy message. It just gives you more months to repeat the same confusion.
posts.direction: Angle: contrarian take on the 'fresh start' instinct — new tactics on top of an unclear foundation don't compound, they clutter. Cover: the temptation to rebrand or pivot vs. the discipline of sharpening what you already have. Audience: owners and ministry leaders who feel the itch to overhaul. Graphic: ig-native — short, punchy, wry observation style.

posts.hook: Your Google Business profile is free real estate. Most organizations leave it half-empty.
posts.direction: Angle: local visibility as stewardship of what you already have. Cover the five fields most organizations skip — hours, description, services/ministry categories, Q&A, and a recent post. Frame it as finishing the work, not chasing an algorithm. Graphic: tip card (numbered list, five items).

posts.hook: Being known in your neighborhood matters more than being seen by strangers on the internet.
posts.direction: Angle: local trust over broad reach. Argue that mission-driven orgs often chase followers in distant markets while neighbors don't know they exist. Real presence — search results, map listings, word of mouth — outlasts any campaign. Craft beats volume. Graphic: quote card, single strong line centered.

posts.hook: Does your online presence match what you actually do for your community? Let's find out.
posts.direction: Angle: gentle audit invitation. Ask the audience to honestly compare their digital footprint to their real-world reputation. CTA: DM or comment 'audit' and we'll take a look together. Keeps the ownership/craftsmanship tone — no pressure, just an honest question. Graphic: ig-native (casual, short, typed-in-app feel).
